page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 32-core custom AWS Graviton processor based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at a dedicated clock rate of 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading, all 32 vCPUs correspond directly to physical cores. The system features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, backed by 36 MB of L3 cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Local storage is provided via 1900 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional memory bandwidth and multi-core throughput for ARM architecture. In memory bandwidth evaluations, uncached large-block reads reach 384.64 GB/sec and writes reach 170.56 GB/sec, placing memory performance in the top tier. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 21489.0 alongside high database operation scores of 46924.96 in PassMark tests and 70.72 million SET operations per second in Redis tests. Software compilation with Clang and multi-threaded decompression also show strong results, whereas single-core processing scores and LLM prompt processing on large 70B parameter models remain in average or lower tiers.

The high resource density of physical CPU cores combined with direct NVMe local storage provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for IO-intensive compute workloads. The primary operational tradeoff stems from the lower RAM ratio per core, which restricts execution of large in-memory datasets or memory-hungry distributed applications. Lacking hardware accelerators such as GPUs, execution of massive machine learning models is constrained. However, the c8gd.8xlarge is exceptionally well suited for high-throughput database workloads, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, and high-frequency key-value caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on a 32-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a dedicated physical core mapping without hyperthreading, the instance delivers high architectural density. Hardware resources include 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 384.64 GB/sec on uncached reads, and excels in database operations and Redis key-value processing. While single-core speeds and large-scale model inference performance remain average, the combination of dedicated ARM cores and direct NVMe storage provides excellent efficiency for IO-heavy computational tasks. Recommended workloads include high-throughput database servers, software build pipelines, web serving, and key-value datastores.
